title: Opt-in SDK migration signals and telemetry-driven rollout for legacy model tags
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Provide a low-friction, opt-in migration pathway for customers using legacy model tags by shipping SDK-level warning flags, telemetry-based reminder nudges, and a staged server-side rollout that ties communications, docs, and sales enablement together.
background: We have a large tail of customers still referencing older model tags (eg. redwood-legacy/v1) causing maintenance overhead and blocking runtime kernel optimizations. Past deprecation efforts were either too blunt or required manual opt-ins. This initiative aims to: 1) reduce blast radius by making the first step an opt-in SDK experience, 2) gather telemetry to identify migration blockers, and 3) coordinate release notes and cross-team GTM so customers are supported throughout the transition.
objectives: Increase voluntary migrations from legacy tags to new stable tags by 35% within 8 weeks of rollout
Collect structured telemetry on top-3 migration blockers across SDKs and surface them to eng within 2 weeks
Ensure release notes, docs, and customer success playbooks are published at least 48 hours before server-side gating begins
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python, Node) ship opt-in warning flag that logs a clear migration hint and an event to telemetry pipeline
Telemetry dashboard shows per-customer migration signals and top failure modes
Cross-functional launch checklist completed and stakeholder sign-off captured in Confluence
Sample migration guide published with code snippets and rollback guidance
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal, 2026-03-20): Engineering dogfood - enable SDK opt-in flag for Redwood internal accounts and 3 pilot customers
Phase 1 (Public opt-in, 2026-04-01): SDKs release 'legacy-migration-preview' flag and release notes announcing opt-in pathway
Phase 2 (Telemetry-driven nudge, 2026-04-15): Automated email and in-console banners to customers who opt-in metric indicates friction, with links to migration wizard

Phase 3 (Server-side soft-gate, 2026-05-01): Begin non-disruptive server-side compatibility warnings; requests from legacy tags will be tagged in logs and receive a structured response header recommending migration
Phase 4 (Final cutover prep, 2026-07-01): Communicate hard dates for any enforced routing fallback if adoption < target; execute only after GTM and CS consensus
communication_plan: Coordinate release notes with Developer Experience: create a single canonical RFC-style doc that feeds into web release notes and SDK changelogs
Draft two email templates (nudge and escalation) for CS to send to affected accounts; include code snippets and support links
Convene weekly 30-min sync between Eng, Docs, CS, and Sales until Phase 3 is complete
Prepare a short in-console banner message and a deeper help center article linked from the banner

stakeholders: Dr. Lena Hoffman - Eng Manager, Runtime
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers ignore opt-in prompts and continue using legacy tags -> Mitigation: CS outreach + account-level telemetry + targeted banner reminders
Risk: Telemetry event schema differs across SDKs -> Mitigation: Define event contract and add automated unit tests + integration smoke tests
Risk: Overwhelming support requests when nudge begins -> Mitigation: CS runbook, prioritized bug triage, and temporary dedicated support hours
Risk: Messaging causes confusion about paid capacity/dedicated customers -> Mitigation: Add explicit bullets in release notes clarifying that this is an opt-in migration and not a pricing change
